post.caption:
Black pepper was used to pay rent, and nutmeg came from a handful of islands worth trading Manhattan for. Before refrigeration, preservation and flavour were genuinely valuable. But the real cost was the chain: a dozen middlemen between the islands and Europe, each taking a cut. Which makes the age of exploration a supply-chain problem in disguise. Columbus sailed west looking for a shortcut to India and hit something else entirely.
